title: Binary Tree Right Side View
statement: Imagine standing on the right side of the tree. Return the values of the nodes you can see, from top to bottom.
hints: The visible node on a level is the last node of that level in a left-to-right BFS.
A DFS that visits the right child before the left child records the first node seen at each depth.
Both answers are the same list.

approaches.name: BFS last node
approaches.explanation: Take the last value of every layer.

approaches.name: Right-first DFS
approaches.explanation: Append when depth equals the answer length.

editorial: Level order already groups the nodes a viewer would scan. The rightmost node of each group is visible. The DFS version relies on visit order: the first time a depth is reached from the right, that node hides everything to its left on the same depth.
reference_solution:
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple
from collections import Counter, OrderedDict, defaultdict, deque

def right_side_view(root: list) -> list[int]:
    levels = level_order(root)
    return [layer[-1] for layer in levels]

examples.explanation: A left child is visible when nothing is to its right.
